```{r load-data}
# Packages
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(ggplot2)
library(bslib)
library(jsonlite)
library(sf)

# Read malaria data
global_raw <- read_csv(
  "Brianna/estimated_number_of_malaria_cases_2000-2015.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

europe_raw <- read_csv(
  "Brianna/estimated_number_of_WHO_europe_malaria_cases_2000-2015.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Read medical doctor data
doctors_raw <- read_csv(
  "Brianna/WHO_global_medical_doctors_per_10,000_(varying_year_ranges).csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Download population estimates from Our World in Data
population_raw <- read.csv(
  "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population-unwpp.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true"
)

# Metadata is retained in case you need to check the population source later.
population_metadata <- fromJSON(
  "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population-unwpp.metadata.json?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true"
)
```

```{r data-prep}
# WHO European Region country ISO3 codes
europe_iso3 <- c(
  "ALB", "AND", "ARM", "AUT", "AZE", "BLR", "BEL",
  "BIH", "BGR", "HRV", "CYP", "CZE", "DNK", "EST",
  "FIN", "FRA", "GEO", "DEU", "GRC", "HUN", "ISL",
  "IRL", "ISR", "ITA", "KAZ", "KGZ", "LVA", "LTU",
  "LUX", "MLT", "MCO", "MNE", "NLD", "MKD", "NOR",
  "POL", "PRT", "MDA", "ROU", "RUS", "SMR", "SRB",
  "SVK", "SVN", "ESP", "SWE", "CHE", "TJK", "TUR",
  "TKM", "UKR", "GBR", "UZB"
)

# Prepare global malaria data.
# Summarising also protects the trend graph from duplicate country-year rows.
global_cases <- global_raw %>%
  transmute(
    iso3 = as.character(SpatialDimValueCode),
    country = as.character(Location),
    year = as.integer(Period),
    cases = as.numeric(FactValueNumeric)
  ) %>%
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2015) %>%
  group_by(iso3, country, year) %>%
  summarise(
    cases = if (all(is.na(cases))) NA_real_ else mean(cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Prepare WHO European malaria data.
# One row per country and year is important for the map join.
europe_cases <- europe_raw %>%
  transmute(
    iso3 = as.character(SpatialDimValueCode),
    country = as.character(country),
    year = as.integer(year),
    cases = as.numeric(FactValueNumeric)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    iso3 %in% europe_iso3,
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2015
  ) %>%
  group_by(iso3, country, year) %>%
  summarise(
    cases = if (all(is.na(cases))) NA_real_ else mean(cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Prepare available-country global trend.
# This is not a complete global total unless every country is represented.
global_trend <- global_cases %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    countries_with_data = sum(!is.na(cases)),
    cases = if (all(is.na(cases))) NA_real_ else sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Prepare WHO European Region trend.
europe_trend <- europe_cases %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    countries_with_data = sum(!is.na(cases)),
    cases = if (all(is.na(cases))) NA_real_ else sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Prepare medical doctor data.
# Values are medical doctors per 10,000 people.
doctors_europe <- doctors_raw %>%
  transmute(
    iso3 = as.character(SpatialDimValueCode),
    year = as.integer(Period),
    doctors_per_10000 = as.numeric(FactValueNumeric)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    iso3 %in% europe_iso3,
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2015
  ) %>%
  group_by(iso3, year) %>%
  summarise(
    doctors_per_10000 = if (all(is.na(doctors_per_10000))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(doctors_per_10000, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Prepare population data from the OWID download.
population_data <- population_raw %>%
  transmute(
    iso3 = as.character(code),
    year = as.integer(year),
    population = as.numeric(
      population__sex_all__age_all__variant_estimates
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    iso3 %in% europe_iso3,
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2015
  ) %>%
  group_by(iso3, year) %>%
  summarise(
    population = if (all(is.na(population))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(population, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Combine malaria cases, doctor availability, and population.
resource_comparison <- europe_cases %>%
  inner_join(
    doctors_europe,
    by = c("iso3", "year")
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    population_data,
    by = c("iso3", "year")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    malaria_per_100000 = (cases / population) * 100000,
    is_azerbaijan = iso3 == "AZE"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(cases),
    !is.na(doctors_per_10000),
    !is.na(malaria_per_100000),
    !is.na(population),
    population > 0
  )

# Prepare map boundaries.
world <- ne_countries(
  scale = "medium",
  returnclass = "sf"
) %>%
  mutate(
    iso3 = if_else(iso_a3 == "-99", adm0_a3, iso_a3)
  ) %>%
  select(iso3, name, geometry)

# Map color palette.
case_palette <- colorNumeric(
  palette = c(
    "#21113D",
    "#63318E",
    "#B536A0",
    "#F15BB5",
    "#FFD166"
  ),
  domain = europe_cases$cases,
  na.color = "#30303A"
)
```

```{r map-functions}
# Prepare map data for the selected year.
make_map_data <- function(selected_year) {

  world %>%
    filter(iso3 %in% europe_iso3) %>%
    left_join(
      europe_cases %>%
        filter(year == as.integer(selected_year)),
      by = "iso3"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      is_azerbaijan = iso3 == "AZE"
    )
}

# Draw the malaria map.
draw_malaria_map <- function(selected_year) {

  map_data <- make_map_data(selected_year)

  # Calculate Azerbaijan's label point in a projected coordinate system.
  azerbaijan_label_point <- map_data %>%
    filter(is_azerbaijan) %>%
    sf::st_transform(6933) %>%
    sf::st_point_on_surface() %>%
    sf::st_transform(4326)

  leaflet(
    map_data,
    options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)
  ) %>%
    addTiles() %>%
    setView(lng = 35, lat = 48, zoom = 3) %>%
    addPolygons(
      group = "country-polygons",
      layerId = ~iso3,
      fillColor = ~case_palette(cases),
      fillOpacity = 0.9,
      color = ~ifelse(is_azerbaijan, "#FF3CAC", "#55515F"),
      weight = ~ifelse(is_azerbaijan, 4, 0.8),
      label = ~paste0(
        name,
        ifelse(is_azerbaijan, " - FOCUS COUNTRY", ""),
        ": ",
        ifelse(
          is.na(cases),
          "No estimate available",
          format(round(cases), big.mark = ",")
        ),
        " Estimated Cases"
      ),
      highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
        weight = 4,
        color = "#FFD166",
        bringToFront = TRUE
      )
    ) %>%
    addLabelOnlyMarkers(
      data = azerbaijan_label_point,
      label = ~"AZERBAIJAN",
      labelOptions = labelOptions(
        noHide = TRUE,
        direction = "top",
        textOnly = TRUE,
        style = list(
          "color" = "#FF3CAC",
          "font-weight" = "bold",
          "font-size" = "12px",
          "text-shadow" = "0 0 5px #000000"
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    addLegend(
      position = "bottomright",
      pal = case_palette,
      values = europe_cases$cases,
      title = "Estimated Cases",
      na.label = "No estimate"
    )
}
```

```{r graph-functions}
# Shared graph appearance.
graph_theme <- function() {

  theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = "#F5F5F7"),
      plot.background = element_rect(
        fill = "#111118",
        color = NA
      ),
      panel.background = element_rect(
        fill = "#111118",
        color = NA
      ),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#30243F"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "#D9CDE8"),
      axis.title = element_text(color = "#D9CDE8"),
      plot.title = element_text(
        color = "#FF3CAC",
        face = "bold",
        size = 14
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#B9B1C9"),
      plot.margin = margin(
        t = 10,
        r = 15,
        b = 10,
        l = 10
      )
    )
}

# Reusable function for the two malaria trend graphs.
make_trend_plot <- function(data, graph_title) {

  ggplot(
    data,
    aes(x = year, y = cases)
  ) +
    geom_line(
      color = "#FF3CAC",
      linewidth = 1.2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    geom_point(
      color = "#FFD166",
      size = 2.5,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = 2000:2015,
      limits = c(2000, 2015)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::comma
    ) +
    labs(
      title = graph_title,
      x = "Year",
      y = "Estimated Malaria Cases"
    ) +
    graph_theme()
}
```

```{r server}
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # Initial map.
  output$malaria_map <- renderLeaflet({
    draw_malaria_map(input$year)
  })

  # Update map polygons when the selected year changes.
  observeEvent(input$year, {

    map_data <- make_map_data(input$year)

    leafletProxy(
      "malaria_map",
      data = map_data
    ) %>%
      clearGroup("country-polygons") %>%
      addPolygons(
        group = "country-polygons",
        layerId = ~iso3,
        fillColor = ~case_palette(cases),
        fillOpacity = 0.9,
        color = ~ifelse(
          is_azerbaijan,
          "#FF3CAC",
          "#55515F"
        ),
        weight = ~ifelse(
          is_azerbaijan,
          4,
          0.8
        ),
        label = ~paste0(
          name,
          ifelse(is_azerbaijan, " - FOCUS COUNTRY", ""),
          ": ",
          ifelse(
            is.na(cases),
            "No estimate available",
            format(round(cases), big.mark = ",")
          ),
          " Estimated Cases"
        ),
        highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
          weight = 4,
          color = "#FFD166",
          bringToFront = TRUE
        )
      )

  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)


  # Available-country global trend graph.
  output$global_trend <- renderPlot({
    make_trend_plot(
      data = global_trend,
      graph_title = "Available Global Malaria Estimates"
    )
  })


  # WHO European Region trend graph.
  output$europe_trend <- renderPlot({
    make_trend_plot(
      data = europe_trend,
      graph_title = "WHO European Region Malaria Estimates"
    )
  })


  # Azerbaijan summary.
  output$azerbaijan_summary <- renderUI({

    az <- europe_cases %>%
      filter(
        iso3 == "AZE",
        year == as.integer(input$year)
      )

    if (nrow(az) == 0 || is.na(az$cases[1])) {
      return(
        p("No estimate available for this year.")
      )
    }

    tagList(

      h4(
        "AZERBAIJAN",
        style = "color:#FF3CAC;"
      ),

      h2(
        format(
          round(az$cases[1]),
          big.mark = ","
        ),
        style = "color:#FFD166;"
      ),

      p("Estimated Malaria Cases"),

      p(
        paste(
          "Selected year:",
          input$year
        )
      )
    )
  })


  # Azerbaijan trend graph.
  output$az_trend <- renderPlot({

    az <- europe_cases %>%
      filter(iso3 == "AZE") %>%
      arrange(year)

    make_trend_plot(
      data = az,
      graph_title = "Azerbaijan: Estimated Malaria Cases"
    )
  })


  # Healthcare resources vs. malaria scatter plot.
  output$resource_scatter <- renderPlot({

    plot_data <- resource_comparison %>%
      filter(year == as.integer(input$year))

    # Show a message instead of attempting to draw an inadequate graph.
    if (nrow(plot_data) < 3) {
      return(
        ggplot() +
          annotate(
            "text",
            x = 0,
            y = 0,
            label = "Not enough countries have matching data for this year.",
            color = "#D9CDE8",
            size = 4
          ) +
          xlim(-1, 1) +
          ylim(-1, 1) +
          labs(
            title = paste(
              "Healthcare Resources vs. Malaria Burden:",
              input$year
            )
          ) +
          graph_theme() +
          theme(
            axis.title = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_blank(),
            panel.grid = element_blank()
          )
      )
    }

    ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(
        x = doctors_per_10000,
        y = malaria_per_100000
      )
    ) +

      # Overall trend line.
      geom_smooth(
        method = "lm",
        formula = y ~ x,
        color = "#FF3CAC",
        linewidth = 1.2,
        se = FALSE
      ) +

      # Country points.
      geom_point(
        aes(color = is_azerbaijan),
        size = 3,
        alpha = 0.85
      ) +

      # Label Azerbaijan only when it is present in the selected year.
      geom_text(
        data = plot_data %>%
          filter(is_azerbaijan),
        aes(label = "Azerbaijan"),
        color = "#FF3CAC",
        nudge_x = 0.1,
        hjust = 0,
        size = 3.5,
        show.legend = FALSE
      ) +

      scale_color_manual(
        values = c(
          "FALSE" = "#FFD166",
          "TRUE" = "#FF3CAC"
        ),
        labels = c(
          "FALSE" = "Other countries",
          "TRUE" = "Azerbaijan"
        ),
        name = "Country"
      ) +

      scale_x_continuous(
        labels = scales::comma
      ) +

      scale_y_continuous(
        labels = scales::comma
      ) +

      labs(
        title = paste(
          "Healthcare Resources vs. Malaria Burden:",
          input$year
        ),
        x = "Medical Doctors per 10,000 People",
        y = "Estimated Malaria Cases per 100,000 People"
      ) +

      graph_theme()
  })


  # Dynamic correlation description.
  output$resource_description <- renderText({

    plot_data <- resource_comparison %>%
      filter(year == as.integer(input$year))

    if (nrow(plot_data) < 3) {
      return(
        "There is not enough matching country data to calculate a correlation for this year."
      )
    }

    # Remove any remaining incomplete observations.
    plot_data <- plot_data %>%
      filter(
        is.finite(doctors_per_10000),
        is.finite(malaria_per_100000)
      )

    if (
      nrow(plot_data) < 3 ||
      length(unique(plot_data$doctors_per_10000)) < 2 ||
      length(unique(plot_data$malaria_per_100000)) < 2
    ) {
      return(
        "A correlation cannot be calculated because there are too few complete observations or one variable has insufficient variation."
      )
    }

    correlation <- cor(
      plot_data$doctors_per_10000,
      plot_data$malaria_per_100000,
      use = "complete.obs",
      method = "pearson"
    )

    if (is.na(correlation)) {
      return(
        "A correlation could not be calculated for this year."
      )
    }

    strength <- if (abs(correlation) < 0.3) {
      "weak"
    } else if (abs(correlation) < 0.7) {
      "moderate"
    } else {
      "strong"
    }

    direction <- if (correlation < 0) {
      "negative"
    } else if (correlation > 0) {
      "positive"
    } else {
      "near-zero"
    }

    paste0(
      "For ",
      input$year,
      ", the relationship between number of medical doctors and Malaria cases is ",
      strength,
      " and ",
      direction,
      ". Pearson correlation: ",
      round(correlation, 2),
      ". This describes an association, meaning it is not evidence that doctor availability causes changes in Malaria cases. The comparison includes ",
      nrow(plot_data),
      " countries with matching data."
    )
  })

}

shinyApp(
  ui = ui,
  server = server
)
```
